stem: The range of a function is the set of $y$-values its graph reaches. Mark the range of $y = 3\sin\theta + 2$ on the $y$-number line, from its lowest value to its highest. Make an end filled if $y$ reaches that value and hollow if it only gets close.
solution: The sine never goes below $-1$ and never above $1$, and it reaches both: $-1 \le \sin\theta \le 1$.
Multiply every part by $3$ (positive, so the inequality signs keep their direction): $-3 \le 3\sin\theta \le 3$.
Add $2$ to every part, because $q = 2$ lifts the whole graph: $-1 \le 3\sin\theta + 2 \le 5$.
So the range is $-1 \le y \le 5$. Mark $-1$ and $5$ with filled circles, since $y$ reaches both values, and shade between them.
notes: Fit: the range is literally a set of y-values with closed ends (the graph attains its lowest and highest values), which is what the interval mode of number_line_marker builds; the question is the book's own multiple choice turned into a construction. The instrument is inside its limits: range [-6,6] is 12 wide, both ends whole numbers inside it, from <= to. Numbers deliberately differ from the book's 2 sin(theta) + 1. Wrong intervals for this question: ignores-added-number gives [-3, 3] (mapped, as the likeliest error); ends-are-the-equation-numbers gives [2, 3]; sine-cosine-start-at-zero gives [2, 5]; adds-q-to-one-end gives [-1, 3] or [-3, 5]. All of them fire the same predicate (interval-wrong), so only the likeliest is mapped and the student who made one of the other three errors will be told about the added number, which is wrong for them. Per-end predicates would split these (see the top-level notes). endpoint-inclusion-wrong (hollow ends) is left unmapped on purpose: this objective's own list has no misconception about inclusion, so that student gets the plain 'not quite'.
